projects.title: IP SHAP
projects.summary: Wholesale drinks storefront for IP SHAP in Kigali: wines, spirits, beer, and soft drinks with cart checkout — orders are confirmed with the shop for availability, delivery, and payment.
projects.audience: Bars, shops, hotels, and buyers in Rwanda who purchase wines, spirits, beer, and soft drinks at wholesale volumes.
scope: Public wholesale catalogue by product range
Cart and checkout with contact and delivery details
Kigali shop presence and contact paths
constraints: No charge on the site until the shop confirms the order
Delivery outside Kigali confirmed case by case
Prices and stock must stay truthful for wholesale buyers
projects.context: IP SHAP sells wholesale wines, spirits, beer, and soft drinks from Kigali. They needed a public site where customers can see ranges and prices, build an order, and leave delivery details — without pretending the site already settles payment.
projects.problem: Wholesale buyers often rely on calls, WhatsApp, or a visit to know what’s available and at what price. That slows ordering and makes it hard to browse the full range before speaking to the shop.
projects.approach: Build a clear catalogue by range (wines & spirits, beer, soft drinks), a standard cart, and a checkout that captures identity and delivery. Keep payment and final confirmation as a human follow-up so stock and logistics stay honest.

decisions.title: Confirm after checkout
decisions.detail: The site collects the order, then IP SHAP confirms availability, delivery, and payment. That keeps wholesale logistics honest instead of promising instant settlement.

decisions.title: Shop by range
decisions.detail: Wines & spirits, beer, and soft drinks are separate entry points so wholesale buyers can scan the shelf they care about first.

decisions.title: Delivery as a conversation
decisions.detail: Coverage and fees outside Kigali are confirmed per order, not hard-coded as a false guarantee.

projects.implementation: Live marketing and ordering site at the-ipshap.com with category browsing, cart, and checkout. Orders trigger a confirm step for availability, delivery coverage, and payment — including areas outside Kigali when agreed.
outcomes: Browsable ranges for wines & spirits, beer, and soft drinks
Checkout that collects order and delivery details for shop confirmation
learnings: For wholesale, trust beats fake instant checkout — confirm stock and payment with the seller.
Clear ranges and “from” pricing help buyers start without a phone call.
projects.notes: Client project. Payment is agreed when the shop confirms the order; the site does not claim instant online settlement.
